content.title: About
content.content: Red bell pepper (Capsicum annuum) is the mature fruit of the sweet pepper plant, harvested raw. It has a bright color, sweet flavor and crisp texture. It is commonly used in fresh salads, side dishes and Asian cuisine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Red peppers reach full maturity, changing from green to red, which boosts their vitamin content.
They belong to the nightshade family and are relatives of chili peppers, but usually contain little capsaicin.
Red peppers contain more antioxidants than their green or yellow counterparts.
In ancient Mediterranean cultures, peppers were grown as ornamental plants and symbols of abundance.
There are over 50 varieties of sweet bell peppers differing in shape, size and shades of red.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Red pepper provides over 150 % of the daily value of vitamin C per 100 g, supporting immunity and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of vitamin A
items.content: Beta‑carotene, which converts to vitamin A, promotes eye health and skin integrity.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Antioxidant phytochemicals
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin protect the eyes from photostress.

items.title: Low‑calorie fiber source
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pepper, such as skin itching or swelling.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Improperly stored peppers can harbor bacteria that cause food poisoning.

items.title: Stomach discomfort
items.content: Large amounts of raw pepper may cause heartburn or discomfort in people with sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat the pepper raw in salads, slice it for snacks, add it to sandwiches, or use it in fresh salsas. It can be lightly sautéed, but raw consumption retains the maximum amount of vitamins.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store peppers in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, in a plastic bag or container. When kept properly they stay fresh for 1‑2 weeks. Discard any peppers that are soft, have spots, or show signs of rot.
